name: Mississippi Today
title: Man said he asked questions about Nolan Wells case, then was jailed
description: Event attendees stand outside holding signs in support of Nolan Wells’ family during a vigil for Wells at Greater St. John AME Church in Biloxi on Wednesday, Aug. 19, 2026.
text:
A New York man accused of making terroristic threats relating to the Nolan Xavier Wells case is now in a Mississippi jail weeks after he said he was just asking questions about the case. People on social media are calling out a lack of transparency about his arrest. 
The Jackson County Sheriff’s Department took Christian Anthony Claudio, 25, into custody after his extradition from Otsego County New York on Saturday. By Monday morning, department officials listed him on its jail docket with a felony charge of making terroristic threats. 
In an affidavit in Jackson County Court uploaded Monday afternoon, Claudio is accused of threatening to travel to Mississippi to kill chancery court clerks “due to findings of a high profile death investigation.” 
He had a first appearance in Jackson County where his bond was set at $50,000, and one of his bond conditions was to stop posting about the case on social media. 
Before his extradition, Claudio, a resident of Oneonta, New York, denied threatening anyone or making “crazy, malicious” statements when he called the Jackson County clerk’s office. 
“I never had no intent, I simply had questions about Nolan Wells, and I had called down there because in my heart, it felt wrong where I was just trying to understand what was going on,” he said in a video call from the Otsego County jail posted Friday on TikTok.
Wells, 18, went missing from Horn Island on July 4. He arrived by boat with friends who departed without him. The friends told investigators that Wells said he would get a ride back on another boat. Two days later, his body was found in waters off the barrier island along Mississippi’s Gulf Coast. On Sept. 21, a Jackson County grand jury declined to indict anyone relating to Wells’ death. 
In a Sunday video, Claudio’s family said he made it to Mississippi and the Jackson County jail, but he doesn’t feel safe there. 
Claudio had been scheduled for a Monday afternoon hearing in New York related to an out-of-state arrest warrant from Mississippi, but Claudio has already been picked up, Cara Tangorra, deputy chief clerk of the Otsego County Court, told Mississippi Today Monday morning. 
If prosecutors gather enough evidence, Claudio could be the sixth person charged with making threats against Jackson County public officials and witnesses tied to Wells’ death investigation. 
Joseph Alfredo Vasquez Dumarce of California plans to plead guilty, according to court records. He is accused of threatening to kill and bomb the office of a Jackson County chancery judge who is the stepmother of one of the friends Wells was last seen with. A man from Illinois who also made threats is scheduled for trial in February.
Claudio was first booked into the Otsego County jail Oct. 31, and he was held there until picked up by Mississippi deputies. 
He began posting on social media shortly after his arrest. Public outcry followed in which people on social media asked to see proof of the phone calls Claudio made to the Jackson County clerk’s office. 
Claudio shared his own account of what happened in a video featuring his sister Nicole Kaura posted Saturday on his TikTok account. Kaura was not immediately available for comment Monday. 
Days after the grand jury’s decision, Claudio called the Jackson County Chancery Clerk’s Office twice to ask a clerk questions about the Wells case. 
Three hours later, her brother received a call from Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter, who asked about Claudio’s calls earlier and if he had any questions about the case. Claudio said he did not. Kaura said Claudio was not told at the time that officials issued a warrant for his arrest. 
On Oct. 30, Claudio went to help a friend who had car issues. Law enforcement who were already at the scene ran his license and found he had an outstanding warrant.
In a Sunday video of that arrest also posted to TikTok, Claudio can be heard asking multiple times about what the warrant is for. 
Kaura said in the video that Sheriff Ledbetter signed the arrest warrant. The warrant alleged Claudio threatened the clerk over the phone and said he would come to Missisisppi.
